Let the net’s vertices be named as follows:

- Upper row: \(A,B,C,D\)
- Lower row: \(F,G,H,E\)
- Top apex: \(J\)
- Bottom apex: \(I\)

Thus the eight triangular faces are
\[
AJB,\ ABF,\ BFG,\ BCG,\ CGH,\ CDH,\ DHE,\ EHI.
\]

An octahedron has three pairs of opposite vertices, denoted
\[
\pm X,\quad \pm Y,\quad \pm Z.
\]
Assign
\[
A=+X,\qquad B=+Y,\qquad F=+Z
\]
in face \(ABF\). Moving across each shared edge, the shared vertices remain fixed while the third vertex changes to its opposite. This gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Face} & \text{Vertices}\\ \hline
AJB & A=+X,\ B=+Y,\ J=-Z\\
BFG & B=+Y,\ F=+Z,\ G=-X\\
BCG & B=+Y,\ C=-Z,\ G=-X\\
CGH & C=-Z,\ G=-X,\ H=-Y\\
CDH & C=-Z,\ D=+X,\ H=-Y\\
DHE & D=+X,\ H=-Y,\ E=+Z\\
EHI & E=+Z,\ H=-Y,\ I=-X
\end{array}
\]

Hence
\[
F\equiv E=+Z,\qquad G\equiv I=-X.
\]

The edge labelled \(5\) is \(FG\), joining \(+Z\) to \(-X\).  
The edge labelled \(x\) is \(EI\), also joining \(+Z\) to \(-X\).

Therefore, when folded, the edge labelled \(x\) joins the edge labelled

\boxed{5}
